prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Conroe, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1373; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. You already have it on the claim.

Q: That's fine. Can you confirm you were the driver of the vehicle involved in the parking lot collision in Conroe, Texas?

A: Yes, I was driving.

Q: Walk me through what happened.

A: I was backing out of a space at the grocery store. I checked my mirrors and didn't see anything, but when I was about halfway out, another car came around the row a little fast and clipped my rear bumper.

Q: Was your vehicle moving at the time of impact?

A: Yes, slowly, maybe a few miles an hour. I hit the brakes right away.

Q: Did you notice any injuries at the scene?

A: Not right away. I felt fine for maybe twenty minutes. Then my neck started to tighten up, and by that evening it was stiff and sore on the left side, down into my shoulder.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or other provider since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next morning. They diagnosed a neck strain and gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and use ice.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Some days are better than others. Turning my head to check blind spots is the hardest part. I've been doing some stretches the therapist showed me.

Q: Did you have any neck problems before this collision?

A: Nothing serious. I had some occasional stiffness from sitting at a desk, but nothing that stopped me from working or sleeping.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get back to normal and get my car repaired.

Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the statement.
